detail.divText: Don’t take it just because it’s new—take it if the role, money, and city move you toward the life you actually want. What’s the one thing making you hesitate?

Don’t compare titles alone—compare the life each choice buys you: take-home pay after housing and moving costs, daily rhythm, growth, and who you’d be leaving behind. A ver, if the practical numbers work, which choice makes you feel more alive rather than merely safer?

Don’t decide from the salary alone—compare growth, cost of living, daily routine, and what you’d be leaving behind. I’d also ask for enough time to picture an ordinary Tuesday there, not just the exciting first month. Which option feels more like moving toward a life you want, rather than merely escaping your current one?
Don’t let a shiny title seduce you—take it only if the move improves your actual life, not just your résumé. What would you gain there that you can’t build where you are?

Don’t judge the offer by salary alone—compare the role, growth, cost of living, support network, and whether the new city fits the life you want. I’d also notice whether the idea feels mostly exciting with manageable fear, or heavy in a way that points to a real mismatch. What would this job give you that your current life can’t?
